name: Dorado Beach, a Ritz Carlton Reserve
positioning: Oceanfront resort in Dorado, Puerto Rico, on the site of Laurance Rockefeller's 1950s resort, operating as a Ritz-Carlton Reserve (official name: Dorado Beach, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve)
best_for: Travelers who want a spa stay with treetop treatments
Couples who like a private treehouse dinner
Guests who enjoy walking or cycling trails along the beach and golf courses

facts.text: Laurance S. Rockefeller opened the resort in the 1950s on a former plantation.
In Rockefeller's original resort, buildings were no taller than palm trees.
Signature dishes at COA restaurant carry the flavor of Mi Brasa, a traditional Spanish wood-burning oven.
A residential kitchen at La Cocina Gourmet hosts hands-on, chef-led cooking classes and five-course themed wine dinners.
Spa Botánico treatments are performed amid gardens and shaded treetops.
Spa Botánico offers a Treehouse Massage amid the treetops.
A 100-year-old Ficus tree stands at the entrance to Spa Botánico.
The resort has two pools, both with direct access to the beach.
Every room is assigned an embajador, a personal butler.
All rooms include indoor and outdoor rainforest showers along with soaking tubs; some also have private plunge pools.

highlights.text: La Cava at COA restaurant is a wine cellar with 690 labels and 3,200 bottles, which the resort describes as the largest wine cellar in Puerto Rico.
In 2012 Ritz-Carlton transformed the resort into its first Reserve property in the Americas.
The Rockefeller Nature Trail is an 11-mile trail that runs past the two golf courses, along sandy beaches and through tree-shaded forests.
The Treehouse Dinner is a private dining experience for two people, usually recommended for couples.
Spa Botánico is a five-acre sanctuary that pairs local Puerto Rican ingredients with indigenous soothing traditions.

considerations.text: The hotel does not provide shuttle service.
Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport is 26.3 miles from the property.
WhataHotel notes limited dining variety compared to larger resort destinations.
